This here is what initially piqued my interest when gg started. As an indie game dev, the fact that there exists this clique of 'cool kids' in indie gaming who have connections with the gaming press really worries me. I don't want connections to trump talent in my industry.

That's already how it is. You don't get a job working on games at a big company because you have more merit than the next guy, you get it because you have connections. The person who knows someone will have an advantage over everyone else all the time in all levels of the industry. It's already broken, certain indie devs getting the ear of "journalists" over other indie devs is only a small symptom of a wider problem in the industry. It's about who you know everywhere, and precious few have broken through that. The most high profile example is The Witcher series. The first one, mainstream games journalism didn't say a peep about it. By Witcher 3, no one could shut up about it.

And herein lies one of the biggest issues I personally have with the industry. I've seen people involved in it ignore, if not flat-out condone the "it's-about-who-you-know" model that exists. Likely because they benefit from such a system. What worries me most about it is that the system in question likely plays a part in why a sizable segment of the industry is such a huge political circlejerk. A lot of social justice-heavy individuals tend to refuse to befriend those who politically disagree with them, which forces such people to either conform to their beliefs, be silent about them completely, or fight a long, uphill battle against an industry that, in many cases, wants nothing to do with them.

This kind of system, regardless of the political affiliations of those who are "in control", is simply inexcusable.
